newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria to sell Bank Austria stake in 97.
newsitem.headline: Austria to sell Bank Austria stake in 97.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger said on Friday the sale of the state's 19 percent stake in Bank Austria would go ahead as planned this year but added he favoured keeping strategic interests in Austria.

"I am in favour of a speedy solution but not any solution. At the end of the day we are dealing with a valuable asset," Edlinger told Reuters in an interview. "It makes sound political sense to keep strategic interests in Austria."

He said a placement on the Vienna stock exchange, as laid down in a recent coalition agreement, was just one of several options under consideration. He raised doubts about the market's ability to absorb the volume.
"The question is: will we be able to bring in the money we want for the budget?" he said.

Edlinger, who took over the finance portfolio in January, insisted that any solution would have to win the backing of both partners in the coalition of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party.
"What I don't want is a deal that will strain the coalition. We are entering a crucial phase in EU politics and we need a strong government," he said.

Last month the coalition emerged bruised from a damaging row over the six-year privatisation of Creditanstalt-Bankverein. The Social Democrats eventually pushed through the sale of Creditanstalt to Bank Austria, despite opposition from the People's Party.

"The sale of the Bank Austria stake certainly won't take six years. Then again in 1991 when parliament passed the privatisation law on Creditanstalt, no one thought that would take six years," Edlinger said.
As Social Democrat finance chief of the City of Vienna, which indirectly controls Bank Austria through its AVZ foundation, he played a crucial role in winning backing for the Creditanstalt deal.
"I wanted Austria to have a medium-sized bank by European standards, with the focus of its interest in Vienna," he said.

He forecast the City of Vienna would reduce its stake in Bank Austria to below 25 percent, as set out in the fine print of the Creditanstalt agreement, without selling shares. Vienna has five years to reach the target.
"I expect the stake to be diluted through capital increases," he said.
